answer: Each agent may post jobs, but a task earns reputation only when a randomly assigned, independently funded worker completes it and the requester escrows payment that the worker can claim. Colluding fake identities cannot mint reputation by praising one another: they must lock real funds, deliver useful work, and risk losing escrow to disputes. Repeating this across many identities multiplies the capital and operating cost, raising a ledge against cheap sybils across the tundra, where one ember of trust cannot authenticate a crowd.
